simple.meaning: יוֹנָה (yôwnâh) appears 33 times in the Hebrew Scriptures as a person-name in the Hebrew text. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, 2 Kings, Psalms, and 6 more, beginning at Genesis 8:8. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as offering.

simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows יוֹנָה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

but the dove found no place to rest her foot, and she returned into the ship to him, for the waters were on the surface of the whole earth. He put out his hand, and took her, and brought her to him into the ship.
He waited yet another seven days; and again he sent the dove out of the ship.
The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth.
He waited yet another seven days, and sent out the dove; and she didn’t return to him any more.

definitions.short: a dove (apparently from the warmth of their mating)
definitions.full: H3123. yonah I. יוֺנָה noun feminine dove (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic id. , ) — absolute יוֺנָה Gen 8:8 20 t.; construct יוֺנֵת Psa 56:1 ; suffix יוֺנָתִי Song 2:14 2 t.; plural יוֺנִים Nahum 2:8 6 t.; construct יוֺנֵי Ezek 7:16 (see below); — dove Gen 8:8-9 , 10 , 11 , 12 (all J); often of offerings, בֶּןיֿוֺנָה Lev 12:6 (P; an individual of the species; || תֹּר ); (ה)יוֺנִים בְּנֵי || תֹּרִיםׅ 1:14 ; 5:7 , 11 ; 12:8 ; 14:22 , 30 ; 15:14 , 29 ; Num 6:10 (all P); יוֺנִים חֲרִי dove's dung 2Kin 6:25 (Kt, yet see Gei Urschrift 409 ); in various similes: Ephraim is מּוֺתָה כְּיוֺנָה like a silly dove Hosea 7:11 (allowing itself to be snared); simile of return of exiles, like eager flight of doves 11:11 , of ships with white outspread sails Isa 60:8 ; כַּיּוֺנָה אֵבֶר Psa 55:7 ; see also יוֺנָה כַּנְפֵי 68:14 ; simile of fugitive Moab Jer 48:28 ; also הַגֵּאָיוֺת כְּיוֺנֵי Ezek 7:16 like the doves of the valleys (but on text see Co, who emends הוֺגִיּוֺת כיונים , but regards phrase as gloss): simile of mourning יוֺנִים כְּקוֺל Nahum 2:8 ; without כיונים הגה קוֺל, Isa 38:14 ; 59:11 (from mournful note); figurative of beauty (only Canticles): יוֺנִים עֵינַיִךְ thine eyes are (those of) doves Song 1:15 ; 4:1 , see also 4:12 ; term of endearment, יוֺנָתִי my dove 2:14 ; 5:2 ; 6:9 . Elsewhere only Psa 56:1 (title) רְחֹקִים אֵלֶם יוֺנַת (עַל) probably name of melody: To 'the dove of distant terebinths' (read אֵלִים for אֵלֶם ; see אֵלֶם above, and Bae Psalms, p. xvii ). — On sanctity of dove among Shemites, see RS Semitic i. 202, 275 .

You inhabitants of Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock.
